newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end up, volume thin on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end up, volume thin on Thursday.

text.p: Singapore shares closed higher on Thursday, but dealers said there was no obvious driver pushing the market up.
"There was a lack of meaningful participation," one local dealer said of the day's trading. He said at best there was some window dressing going on.
That seemed to work though as the Straits Times Industrials Index rose 10.55 points to end the day at 2,197.69.
Market volume across the Singapore market was tiny, however, with just 25.7 million units traded on the day.
Dealers said more active trade had occurred in Malaysia.
"Malaysian stocks are the exciting place to be at the moment," said a local dealer.
This sentiment appeared to be reflected in rise in the broader-based Business Times-Singapore Regional Index, which climbed 7.25 to 1,091.72.
Singapore-listed Thai telecommunications firm Total Access Communications was the day's biggest gainer, up US$0.35 to US$6.90.
The day's biggest fall came for investment fund stock, Thai Prime, which slipped US$0.30 to US$12.10.
